settings_tokens_whole_account_title: A token is the whole account
settings_tokens_whole_account_body: A token authenticates as its owner and inherits their role and organisation. There is no narrower permission to give it. Issue one per integration so a single revocation stops a single thing, set an expiry, and revoke anything you cannot name a use for. The value is shown once when the token is created and cannot be recovered afterwards.

settings_inbound_explain_off: Mail still arrives here and no ticket is opened. Nothing bounces, so whoever wrote gets silence rather than an error.

settings_inbound_address_hint: Mail to the old address stops becoming tickets.

settings_inbound_topic_hint: Mail is accepted only from this exact topic. Left blank, it is set by the first subscription AWS confirms from an AWS account this server allows. Clearing it stops mail until it is set again.

settings_inbound_active_hint: Starts creating tickets from mail to this address as soon as it is saved.

settings_inbound_silent_many: {addresses} are switched on and create nothing

settings_inbound_turn_off_explain: Stops opening tickets from this address. It stays in the list, off, until turned back on.
settings_inbound_delete_explain: Deleted permanently. Mail to this address stops becoming tickets, and its topic pin goes with it.
settings_inbound_genuine_title: How a delivery is proved genuine
settings_inbound_genuine_body: Two checks, and mail has to clear both: AWS signs each notification, and the address has to be pinned to the exact SNS topic it was subscribed to. The signature alone proves only that some AWS account sent it, so without the pin anyone who learned an address's id could have AWS sign forged mail into this organisation. An admin can enter the pin as the address's Topic ARN. Left blank, it is set by the first subscription AWS confirms from an AWS account this server allows; a subscription from any other account is refused. Only admins can see the ARN, because it carries the AWS account id.
settings_inbound_secret_body: A Postmark or Mailgun address is proved by a secret an admin stores on it instead: Postmark's basic-auth password or Mailgun's signing key. With none stored, every post is refused. It is never readable back, here or anywhere.

settings_hours_always_on_body: A four-hour target expires four hours after the ticket arrives, weekend or not. The engine drops a calendar that never opens rather than treating it as permanently shut, so open at least one day to make this calendar count.

settings_hours_changes_always_on: With no day open, targets do not count anything out: they run on the wall clock, through evenings, weekends and the holidays below.
settings_hours_changes_monday: Response and resolution targets count only the time inside these hours. A ticket opened at 17:20 on Friday starts its clock at {time} on Monday, so the weekend does not spend a four-hour target.
settings_hours_changes_next_open: Response and resolution targets count only the time inside these hours. A ticket opened at 17:20 on Friday starts its clock whenever the week next opens, so the weekend does not spend a four-hour target.

settings_webforms_warning_title: A published form accepts posts from anyone
settings_webforms_warning_body: It has to: the whole point is that a stranger can fill it in without an account. A honeypot field, per-form and per-address rate limits, and disposable-address rejection are always on, and each form can add a Cloudflare Turnstile challenge of its own. Publish only the forms you are embedding, and unpublish one the moment you take its snippet off your site.

settings_webhooks_forbidden_list: Webhooks send copies of this organization's records to other services, and a hook URL is often a secret of its own, so only admins can see or change them.
settings_webhooks_forbidden_detail: Webhooks send copies of this organization's records to other services, so only admins can see or change them.

settings_webhooks_empty_body: A webhook posts to a URL whenever a {kinds} changes. Point one at Zapier, n8n, Slack or your own code.
settings_webhooks_sig_title: Check the signature before trusting a delivery
settings_webhooks_sig_body: Every JSON delivery carries an {header} header: an HMAC-SHA256 of the timestamp and the raw body, keyed with the webhook's secret. A failed delivery is retried five times over about eight and a half hours, and an endpoint that answers 410 Gone is paused. So is every webhook whose creator stops being an admin, is deactivated or leaves; any admin can turn it back on and then answers for it. The Webhooks page in the documentation has verification code and Zapier and n8n recipes.

settings_webhooks_description_placeholde: e.g. Zapier: new leads to the sales sheet

settings_lead_capture_delete_explain: The URL stops working at once and its delivery log goes with it. Leads it made stay.
settings_lead_capture_switched_off_note: Switched off: posts to the URL are refused, answered as if it did not exist.
settings_lead_capture_owner_hint: A lead that matches one already here keeps its owner. To share new leads out in turn, use an automation rule.
settings_lead_capture_fields_hint: Name each field by its path in the post, with dots between levels, for example {example}. A field no row uses goes into the lead's enquiry text, so nothing anyone typed is lost.
settings_lead_capture_deliveries_hint: The newest 50 posts, accepted or refused. Posts are kept for 30 days.
settings_lead_capture_deliveries_failed: The deliveries could not be loaded. Refresh to try again.
settings_lead_capture_deliveries_none: Nothing has arrived yet. Send a test, or post a lead from the tool.
settings_apps_sub: Install an industry app to set BottleCRM up for one kind of business, and switch off the modules this organization does not use. Neither ever deletes a record.
settings_apps_forbidden: Only an organization admin can install apps or switch modules on or off.
settings_apps_done_remove_note: Every record stays, and installing it again brings its parts back.
settings_apps_status_removed: Removed. Installing it again brings its parts back.
settings_apps_load_failed: Apps could not be loaded. Reload the page to try again.
settings_apps_none_available: No industry apps are available right now.
settings_apps_lede_remove: Its fields are turned off and its lead sources and products made inactive. Pipelines, tags and every record stay. Installing it again brings it all back.
settings_apps_lede_upgrade: Only what is new is added. Nothing this organization already has changes.
settings_apps_lede_install: This is everything it adds. Anything already here is kept as it is.
settings_apps_sample_hint: Marked as samples, so "Clear sample data" below removes them.
settings_private_apps_removed: Removed {name}. Every record stays; install it again from the list below.
settings_private_apps_empty: No apps of your own yet. Upload the file for one below; you will see what it adds before anything is installed.
settings_private_apps_upload_lede: A .json file, or paste its text. A new version of an app you have installed updates it.
settings_private_apps_forbidden: Only an organization admin can install apps.
settings_private_apps_no_access_key_stop: It asks for no access. Its key stops working.
settings_private_apps_no_access_no_key: It asks for no access. No key is made.
